topic: Separating Data Movement Evaluation from Micro-Execution Overhead
principle: When benchmarking VMs or interpreters that manipulate large data structures, isolate the cost of data movement (allocation, copying, transfers) from the cost of actual computation (micro-executions). Zero-copy benchmarks should measure only the execution engine's overhead, not the memory management costs that are orthogonal to instruction semantics.
instruction: When designing benchmarks for a Tensor VM or similar data-intensive execution engine, factor out data movement costs by using zero-copy references or pre-allocated buffers, ensuring the benchmark measures pure execution throughput rather than memory allocation patterns.
